en: Ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Kulayb, who said: I heard Abu Burdah say: I heard 'Ali ibn Abi Talib say: "He forbade"—or "He forbade me"—meaning the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he mentioned something similar to it.

Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Kulayb, from a son of Abu Musa, who said: I heard 'Ali... and he mentioned this hadith from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) with something similar to it.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr and Abu Kurayb narrated to me, both from Ibn Idris—and the wording is Abu Kurayb's—Ibn Idris narrated to us, he said: I heard 'Asim ibn Kulayb, from Abu Burdah, from 'Ali, who said: He—meaning the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—forbade me from placing my ring on this finger or the one next to it ('Asim did not know which of the two), and he forbade me from wearing al-qassi garments and from sitting on mayathir cushions. He said: As for al-qassi, they are ribbed garments brought from Egypt and Syria having such silk-like stripes; and as for mayathir, they were things that women made for their husbands to put on saddles, like purple velvets.

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ibrahim ibn 'Abdullah ibn Hunayn, from his father, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade me from wearing a gold ring, from wearing al-qassi garments, from reciting Quran while bowing (ruku') and prostrating (sujud), and from wearing saffron-dyed (mu'asfar) garments.

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, Ibrahim ibn 'Abdullah ibn Hunayn narrated to me that his father narrated to him that he heard 'Ali ibn Abi Talib saying: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade me from reciting Quran while I am bowing, and from wearing gold and saffron-dyed garments.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: I read to Malik, from Nafi', from Ibrahim ibn 'Abdullah ibn Hunayn, from his father, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade wearing al-qassi garments, wearing saffron-dyed garments, wearing a gold ring, and reciting the Quran while bowing.

Dawud ibn Rushayd narrated to us, 'Umar ibn Ayyub al-Mawsili narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Nafi' narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Ahwal, from Tawus, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saw two saffron-dyed garments on me, so he said: "Did your mother command you to wear this?" I said: "Shall I wash them?" He said: "Rather, burn them."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Hisham informed us; (H) and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn al-Mubarak, both from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, with this chain of narration, and both said: "from Khalid ibn Ma'dan."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Yahya, Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith narrated to me that Ibn Ma'dan informed him that Jubayr ibn Nufayr informed him that 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As informed him, saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saw two saffron-dyed garments on me and said: "Indeed, these are among the garments of the disbelievers, so do not wear them."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me, 'Affan narrated to us, Hammam narrated to us, Qatadah narrated to us that Anas informed him that 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf and al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam complained to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) of lice, so he granted them concession to wear silk shirts during an expedition of theirs.
Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated it to us, they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, with this chain of narration, the like of it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) granted concession—or concession was granted—to al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf to wear silk because of an itching they had.
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it to us, Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, with this chain of narration, and he did not mention: "on a journey."

Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, Qatadah narrated to us that Anas ibn Malik informed them that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) granted concession to 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf and al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam to wear silk shirts on a journey because of an itching they had or an ailment they had.
Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated it to us, al-Dahhak—meaning Abu 'Asim—narrated to us, 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Yazid ibn Abi Habib narrated to me, with this chain of narration.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu al-Khayr, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, that he said: A silk farruj (a tunic-like outer robe with a slit back) was gifted to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). He wore it and prayed in it; then after completing the prayer he pulled it off violently as one who loathed it, and said: "This is not befitting for the pious."

Ibrahim ibn Musa al-Razi narrated to me, Shu'ayb ibn Ishaq al-Dimashqi informed us, from al-Awza'i, Shaddad Abu 'Ammar narrated to me, Abu Umamah narrated to me, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever wears silk in this world will not wear it in the Hereafter."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us, they said: Isma'il—who is Ibn 'Ulayyah—narrated to us, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Suhayb, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever wears silk in this world will not wear it in the Hereafter."

Shayban ibn Farrukh and Abu Kamil narrated to us—and the wording is Abu Kamil's—they said: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Asamm, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) sent 'Umar a cloak of sundus (fine silk). 'Umar said: "You sent it to me when you said concerning it what you said?" He said: "I did not send it to you for you to wear it; I only sent it to you so that you might benefit from its price."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Ghundar narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Maysarah, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) clothed me with a silken-striped suit (hullah siyara'). I went out wearing it, and I saw anger on his face—he said—so I tore it into pieces among my womenfolk.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Kurayb, and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us—and the wording is Zuhayr's—Abu Kurayb said: "informed us," and the other two said: "Waki' narrated to us," from Mis'ar, from Abu 'Awn al-Thaqafi, from Abu Salih al-Hanafi, from 'Ali, that Ukaydir of Dumah gifted a silk garment to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he gave it to 'Ali and said: "Tear it into head-coverings (khumur) among the Fatimahs." And Abu Bakr and Abu Kurayb said: "among the women."

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated it to us, my father narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Muhammad—meaning Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us, both saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu 'Awn, with this chain of narration; in the hadith of Mu'adh: "so he ordered me and I divided it into veils among my womenfolk," and in the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ja'far: "so I divided it into veils among my womenfolk," and he did not mention: "so he ordered me."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman—meaning Ibn Mahdi—narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu 'Awn, who said: I heard Abu Salih narrating from 'Ali, who said: A silken-striped suit (hullah siyara') was gifted to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he sent it to me. So I wore it, but I recognized anger in his face, whereat he said: "I did not send it to you for you to wear it; I only sent it to you so that you could tear it into head-coverings (khumur) among the women."

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali, Yahya ibn Habib, and Hajjaj ibn al-Sha'ir narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn Habib's—Ishaq said: "informed us," and the others said: "Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us," Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah say: One day the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) wore an outer gown (qaba') of brocade that had been gifted to him, but he quickly took it off and sent it to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. It was said to him: "How quickly you took it off, O Messenger of Allah!" He said: "Gabriel forbade me from it." Then 'Umar came to him weeping and said: "O Messenger of Allah, you disliked a thing yet gave it to me; what should I do?" He said: "I did not give it to you for you to wear it; I only gave it to you so that you could sell it." So he sold it for two thousand dirhams.
Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah al-Ruzzi narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' informed us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, with this chain of narration, the like of it.

'Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar al-Qawariri, Abu Ghassan al-Misma'i, Zuhayr ibn Harb, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us—Ishaq said: "informed us," and the others said: "narrated to us"—Mu'adh ibn Hisham, my father narrated to me, from Qatadah, from 'Amir al-Sha'bi, from Suwayd ibn Ghafalah, that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab delivered a sermon at al-Jabiyah and said: The Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade the wearing of silk except the space of two fingers, or three, or four.

Abu Ghassan al-Misma'i and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, they said: Mu'adh—who is Ibn Hisham—narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Qatadah, with this chain of narration, the like of it, and he did not mention the statement of Abu 'Uthman.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: I heard Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi say: A letter from 'Umar reached us while we were in Azerbaijan with 'Utbah ibn Farqad—or in Syria—stating: "To proceed: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade silk except like this: two fingers." Abu 'Uthman said: "We had no doubt that he meant the border-patterns (a'lam)."
Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father, Abu 'Uthman narrated to us, who said: We were with 'Utbah ibn Farqad... with the like of the hadith of Jarir.

Ibn Abi Shaybah—who is 'Uthman—and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali narrated to us, both from Jarir—and the wording is Ishaq's—Jarir informed us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu 'Uthman, who said: We were with 'Utbah ibn Farqad when 'Umar's letter reached us, stating that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "None wears silk except one who has no portion of it in the Hereafter, except like this." And Abu 'Uthman indicated with his two fingers that follow the thumb. Abu 'Uthman said: "I thought they were like the borders of Persian cloaks (tayalisah) when I saw Persian cloaks."
